input.pr_title: feat: add rate limiting to content submission endpoint
input.pr_description:
Adds sliding-window rate limiting to prevent spam content submissions.

## Changes
- New RateLimiter utility class with in-memory sliding window
- Rate limit dependency injected into content creation endpoint
- Returns 429 with Retry-After header when limit exceeded
- Default: 5 submissions per 60 seconds per user
input.bugged_diff:
diff --git a/app/utils/rate_limiter.py b/app/utils/rate_limiter.py
new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/app/utils/rate_limiter.py
@@ -0,0 +1,35 @@
+import time
+
+
+class RateLimiter:
+    def __init__(self, max_requests: int = 5, window_seconds: int = 60):
+        self.max_requests = max_requests
+        self.window_seconds = window_seconds
+        self._requests: dict[str, list[float]] = {}
+
+    def is_allowed(self, key: str) -> tuple[bool, dict]:
+        now = time.time()
+        if key not in self._requests:
+            self._requests[key] = []
+
+        # Filter expired timestamps
+        self._requests[key] = [
+            ts for ts in self._requests[key] if now - ts < self.window_seconds
+        ]
+
+        remaining = self.max_requests - len(self._requests[key])
+        if remaining > 0:
+            self._requests[key].append(now)
+            return True, {
+                "limit": self.max_requests,
+                "remaining": remaining - 1,
+                "retry_after": 0,
+            }
+        else:
+            oldest = self._requests[key][0]
+            retry_after = self.window_seconds - (now - oldest)
+            return False, {
+                "limit": self.max_requests,
+                "remaining": 0,
+                "retry_after": round(retry_after),
+            }
+

planted_defects.title: Rate limit key uses only user_id — all endpoints share one counter
planted_defects.description: The rate limit key is `current_user.id`, which means ALL rate-limited endpoints share a single counter per user. If the user hits the content creation limit (5 requests), they'll also be blocked from other rate-limited endpoints. The key should include the endpoint path to isolate counters per endpoint, e.g., `f'content_create:{current_user.id}'`.
planted_defects.root_cause: The call `limiter.is_allowed(current_user.id)` uses a bare user ID without endpoint-specific scoping.
planted_defects.suggested_fix: Change to `limiter.is_allowed(f'content_create:{current_user.id}')` to scope the counter to this specific endpoint.

planted_defects.title: Rate limiter failure crashes the request instead of graceful degradation
planted_defects.description: The rate limiting code has no try/except around the limiter call. If the rate limiter throws any exception (KeyError, AttributeError, or in production a Redis ConnectionError), the entire request fails with a 500 error. Rate limiting is a secondary concern — if it fails, the request should proceed without rate limiting (fail-open) rather than blocking the user entirely.
planted_defects.root_cause: No exception handling around `limiter.is_allowed()`. In production with Redis, network failures would crash every request that has rate limiting.
planted_defects.suggested_fix: Wrap the rate limit check in try/except: `try: allowed, info = limiter.is_allowed(...) except Exception: allowed = True`. Log the error for monitoring.
